fit.gap_handling_summary: The CV presents a strong and credible stack match, supported by measurable mobile performance, accessibility remediation, API integration and regulated fintech work. It correctly preserves WCAG 2.1 rather than claiming 2.2, limits Next.js to marketing pages, and does not invent healthcare, GDPR or OWASP experience. Health-data learning motivation is not addressed, while semantic/responsive implementation, design-system depth and analytics remain less explicit than the core engineering evidence.

issues: The GitHub identifier is supplied, but a full profile or selected project URL would make the optional work sample easier to access.
Skills, mentoring and languages are all on the relatively sparse second page; the page balance could be improved.
The summary repeats 'customer-facing' within the same sentence.

keywords_missing_but_candidate_has: authentication — BankID identity-verification integration is relevant evidence, though the CV uses identity-verification wording rather than this exact keyword
reasons: The PDF extracts in sensible reading order with intact words and conventional section headings.
The core React/TypeScript, Node/NestJS, PostgreSQL, cloud and testing stack is explicitly represented.
Professional experience substantially exceeds the minimum and is linked to dated roles.
WCAG 2.1 AA is a close, honestly labelled accessibility match, not evidence of the exact 2.2 standard.
Missing privacy and OWASP terms could reduce ranking in a highly keyword-driven screen, but those competencies should not be invented.

issues: Company tailoring is accurate but light: it refers to accessible, straightforward patient experiences without using a distinctive product, recent development or company principle explicitly.
The document-upload sentence combines several technical achievements, accessibility remediation and performance into one dense sentence.
It mainly repeats CV evidence rather than explaining the transition from fintech onboarding to patient-facing software.
It does not discuss learning health-data privacy requirements or distinguish the candidate's WCAG 2.1 experience from Verdane's 2.2 target.
strengths: Correct company, role and squad throughout.
Strong, supported evidence covering the frontend, backend, database, testing and accessibility requirements.
Uses concrete conversion and performance results rather than generic self-praise.
Accurately presents current NestJS experience instead of reusing the earlier letter's outdated desire to learn it.
Concise, professional English with contact details and GitHub identifier.

culture_used: Straightforward software, consistent with 'Simple beats clever'
Focus on the people using the product

spacing_issues: The CV is noticeably unbalanced: page one is dense, while page two is only 37.7% filled and leaves a large blank lower area.
The CV section rules sit very close to the heading baseline and visually run through the lower edge of some heading letters.
issues: The serif typography, margins and restrained styling are consistent across the set.
The large name heading and bold role headings establish a clear hierarchy, but rebalancing content would make the two-page CV feel more deliberate.
The cover letter is comfortably readable on one page; its blank lower area is normal for a short letter.

fluency_and_tone_issues: CV: 'customer-facing applications ... customer-facing experiences' is repetitive within one summary sentence.

Cover letter: 'I also built a secure document-upload flow ... remediated WCAG 2.1 AA audit findings and helped improve mobile LCP ...' is grammatical but overloaded; splitting it would improve readability.

notes_facts_used: Frontend is the candidate's strongest area.
Four months as acting team lead in 2024, with one-to-ones and sprint planning.
GraphQL is described as maintaining a shared BFF, not as deep expertise.
notes_facts_ignored: The desired senior full-stack or senior frontend positioning is not explicit in the headline, although the experience and temporary leadership are shown.

parsed.summary: This is a credible, well-targeted application with supported achievements and a strong React/TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL, testing and AWS match. It handles experience boundaries carefully, including temporary leadership, shared GraphQL maintenance, marketing-only Next.js and WCAG 2.1 rather than 2.2. The principal content improvements are a more distinctive company motivation, clearer discussion of the health-data learning transition, and inclusion of relevant Redis experience. Both PDFs are readable and parse cleanly, though the CV's dense first page and sparse second page would benefit from rebalancing.
